identity.name: Guiyi Circuit
alt_names: Dunhuang Kingdom of the Western Han

land.text: Shazhou and Guazhou, taken from Tibetan control in 848; Ganzhou, Suzhou, Yizhou, Xizhou and Liangzhou followed

predecessors.note: The Tibetan Empire had split in 842; the Tibetan garrisons of the Hexi corridor are the 'tibetans' dossier's land. Cliopatria has no row for the Guiyi.

land.text: Shazhou and Guazhou; 'the Tanguts, who later founded Western Xia, annexed the kingdom' in 1036

successors.note: Cao Xianshun surrendered to the Tanguts in 1030; the annexation is 1036. By the end of the 10th century the circuit kept only Guazhou and Shazhou (Guiyi page).

capitals.name: Shazhou (Dunhuang)
capitals.note: 'Capital: Shazhou (modern Dunhuang), usually'; Xuanzong named the eleven prefectures 'Guiyi Circuit, with its capital at Sha Prefecture' (Zhang Yichao page).

rulers.name: Zhang Yichao
rulers.title: jiedushi (military commissioner)
rulers.note: Rose at Shazhou in 848; went to Chang'an in 867 and died there in 872.

rulers.name: Zhang Chengfeng
rulers.title: jiedushi; Emperor Baiyi of the Jinshan Kingdom 910-914
rulers.note: Grandson of Zhang Yichao; the page gives 909-911 for the Jinshan Kingdom in the lead and 910 in the body.

rulers.name: Cao Yijin
rulers.title: military commissioner; Great King-reclaiming-the-west from 931
rulers.note: Abolished the kingdom in 914 (the page gives 914, not 920).

rulers.name: Cao Yanlu
rulers.note: Died by suicide after his nephew Cao Zongshou rebelled in 1002.

rulers.name: Cao Xianshun
rulers.note: Surrendered to the Tanguts in 1030; the annexation is 1036.

correction.text: Shazhou (Dunhuang) and Guazhou, retaken from Tibetan control by Zhang Yichao's uprising of 848

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page names the two prefectures; the 200 km circle round Dunhuang is the researcher's reading (the Tang dossier uses the same). The Zhang Yichao page has Zhang attack the other ten prefectures 'later in the year' 848 without dating each; the Guiyi page's own dates (850, 851) are used. Neither page gives an area.

correction.text: Shazhou and Guazhou with Ganzhou (Zhangye), Suzhou (Jiuquan) and Yizhou (Hami), captured by 850

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'Zhang had captured Ganzhou, Suzhou, and Yizhou' by 850. Circles are the researcher's reading of the prefectures.

correction.text: the above plus Xizhou (Gaochang), taken in 851, when the Tang court named the territory the Guiyi Circuit

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The Zhang Yichao page lists eleven prefectures named by the court (Sha, Gua, Gan, Su, Yi, Xi, Lan, Shan, He, Min, Kuo); the Guiyi page extends authority to the last five only in 861, so they are added then. Neither page gives an area.

correction.text: the western seven prefectures plus Lanzhou, Shanzhou, Hezhou, Minzhou and Kuozhou, the 'eleven prefectures' of the Guiyi Circuit

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. '861: authority extended to Guazhou, Ganzhou, Suzhou, Yizhou, Lanzhou, Shanzhou, Hezhou, Minzhou, Liangzhou, and Kuozhou'. The five eastern prefectures are drawn from Lanzhou, Xining, Linxia and Minxian; the page names no frontier. The Zhang Yichao page gives no later fate for them.

correction.text: the eleven prefectures plus Liangzhou, captured by Zhang Yichao in 863

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'In 863, Zhang Yichao led a group of 7,000 Han and non-Han soldiers to capture Liang Prefecture' (the Guiyi page lists Liangzhou in the 861 extent; the Tang and Tibetan dossiers date it 861).

correction.text: as before without Xizhou, which the Uyghurs took in 866

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. '866: ... The Uyghurs took Xizhou.' Zhang also 'briefly seized Luntai and Tingzhou, which Qocho soon recaptured'.

correction.text: as before without Yizhou (Hami), lost in 876

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. '876: Yizhou was lost (the sources differ on whether Qocho or the Xizhou Uyghurs took it)'.

correction.text: Shazhou, Guazhou and Suzhou after Ganzhou and Liangzhou 'slipped from Guiyi control' in 881-882

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The five eastern prefectures (Lan, Shan, He, Min, Kuo) have no dated loss on either page; they are dropped here at confidence 1 (ledger 882). The Ganzhou Uyghur Kingdom held Ganzhou 'by 894' and Xiliangfu held Liangzhou 'by 906'. Suzhou is kept through to 999 as a reading: the Guiyi page names it only for 850 and 861 and says the circuit by the end of the 10th century kept only Guazhou and Shazhou, and the Ganzhou page lists Suzhou among the places where Uyghur remnants settled without a date.

correction.text: Shazhou, Guazhou and Suzhou plus Yizhou and Xizhou, occupied from Qocho by Zhang Chengfeng from 904 (the Jinshan Kingdom from 910)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. '904: Zhang Chengfeng attacked Qocho and seized Yizhou and Xizhou.' The Qocho page calls it an occupation and ends it in 911 ('after the Jinshan Kingdom's loss to the Ganzhou Uyghur Kingdom in 911'), so the keyframe runs 904-910.

correction.text: Shazhou, Guazhou and Suzhou after the occupation of Yizhou and Xizhou ended in 911 (the Jinshan Kingdom to 914, then the Cao family)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Yizhou and Xizhou go in 911, the year the Qocho page ends the occupation; the Guiyi page gives no loss date. Suzhou stays as a reading: the Guiyi page says only that 'by the end of the 10th century it was only able to keep the prefectures of Guazhou and Shazhou' and does not date the loss of Suzhou; the Ganzhou page puts Uyghur remnants in Suzhou and the Jiuquan page says it 'was controlled by the Ganzhou Uyghur Kingdom' (no year) and was seized by Xixia in 1028. The Ganzhou Kingdom shape overlaps this Suzhou circle until 999 (the two dossiers draw the same land for those years).

correction.text: Shazhou and Guazhou, the only prefectures the Guiyi still kept 'by the end of the 10th century'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'By the end of the 10th century it was only able to keep the prefectures of Guazhou and Shazhou' (Rong Xinjiang, as quoted on the page); the loss of Suzhou is entered at the latest year that sentence allows, 1000, at confidence 1. The Ganzhou page has the Guazhou Uyghurs surrender to the Tanguts in 1030 and Shazhou in 1036. No area is given on either page.

ledger.note: 848: Zhang Yichao raises Shazhou against Tibet. 'Zhang Yichao led an uprising in Shazhou and took Shazhou and Guazhou from Tibetan control.' The Tibetan garrisons fled and Xuanzong made him Official Guard of Sha Prefecture (Zhang Yichao page).

850: Ganzhou, Suzhou and Yizhou. 'By 850 Zhang had captured Ganzhou, Suzhou, and Yizhou' from the Tibetan garrisons; the Zhang Yichao page has the attack on ten more prefectures 'later in the year' 848 without dates.

851: the Tang court names the Guiyi Circuit. 'The Tang court named the territory Guiyi Prefecture and made Zhang Yichao Guiyi Jiedushi'; infobox 851-1036, 'usually de facto independent, nominally subordinate to the Tang, the Five Dynasties, and the Northern Song'. The Tang dossier carries the vassal tint from 851.

region.text: Lanzhou, Shanzhou, Hezhou, Minzhou and Kuozhou

ledger.note: 861: authority over the eastern prefectures. 'Authority extended to Guazhou, Ganzhou, Suzhou, Yizhou, Lanzhou, Shanzhou, Hezhou, Minzhou, Liangzhou, and Kuozhou.' The five eastern ones (Lan, Shan, He, Min, Kuo) were named among the eleven prefectures of the circuit on the Zhang Yichao page; their place in the field is the researcher's reading.
863: Liangzhou taken. 'In 863, Zhang Yichao led a group of 7,000 Han and non-Han soldiers to capture Liang Prefecture' (Wuwei). The Guiyi page puts Liangzhou in the extent of 861.

866: Xizhou lost. 'The Uyghurs took Xizhou' (the Zhang Yichao page has Zhang report that the Uyghur chieftain Pugu Jun recaptured Xi Prefecture from Tibet, implying he acted under Zhang's command); Zhang also 'briefly seized Luntai and Tingzhou, which Qocho soon recaptured'.
876: Yizhou lost. 'Yizhou was lost (the sources differ on whether Qocho or the Xizhou Uyghurs took it).'

881-882: Ganzhou and Liangzhou slip away. 'Ganzhou and Liangzhou slipped from Guiyi control. The Ganzhou Uyghurs established their kingdom there by 894, and the Tibetan state of Xiliangfu held Liangzhou by 906.' The span 881-882 is rounded to 882; the page names no new holder in that year.

region.text: Lanzhou, Shanzhou, Hezhou, Minzhou and Kuozhou (no page dates their loss)

ledger.note: 882: the eastern prefectures drop out (page silent). Lanzhou, Shanzhou, Hezhou, Minzhou and Kuozhou are listed for 861 and the Zhang Yichao page gives them no later fate; bridging at the one dated shrinkage of the 880s.

904: Yizhou and Xizhou occupied. 'Zhang Chengfeng attacked Qocho and seized Yizhou and Xizhou.' Typed as an occupation to agree with the Qocho dossier (occupation 904-911, counterpart guiyi-circuit); the Qocho page calls it an occupation.

910: the Jinshan Kingdom. 'Zhang Chengfeng declared himself Emperor Baiyi and renamed the prefecture the Jinshan Kingdom' (Western Han Jinshan); the lead gives 909-911, which conflicts with the body. In 911 the Ganzhou Uyghurs forced it into 'a subordinate alliance': 'the Khan is the father, and the Son of Heaven is the son.'

911: the occupation of Yizhou and Xizhou ends. 'This occupation ended after the Jinshan Kingdom's loss to the Ganzhou Uyghur Kingdom in 911' (Qocho page); mirror of qocho-kingdom 911. The Guiyi page gives no date for the loss after 904 and says only that the Ganzhou Uyghurs forced the Jinshan Kingdom into 'a subordinate alliance' in 911.

914: the Cao family restores the Guiyi. 'Cao Yijin took the throne, abolished the kingdom, and restored Guiyi Prefecture, calling himself military commissioner' (the page gives 914, not 920); the Later Liang confers the title in 918.

1000 at the latest: Suzhou leaves the Guiyi. 'By the end of the 10th century it was only able to keep the prefectures of Guazhou and Shazhou' (Rong Xinjiang, as quoted on the page); the page does not name Suzhou or date its loss. The Ganzhou page lists Suzhou among the places where Uyghur remnants settled and the Jiuquan page says it 'was controlled by the Ganzhou Uyghur Kingdom' before Xixia seized it in 1028, so the Ganzhou Uyghurs are the likely holder; the year is a bridge, and the ganzhou-kingdom dossier has no matching gain.

1036: the Tanguts annex the Guiyi. 'In 1030 Cao Xianshun surrendered to the Tanguts' and 'In 1036 the Tanguts, who later established the Western Xia, annexed the Kingdom of Guiyi'; the page keeps only Guazhou and Shazhou by the end of the 10th century and does not say which prefectures fell in 1036. The Ganzhou page has the Guazhou Uyghurs surrender in 1030 and Shazhou in 1036.

wars.name: Zhang Yichao uprising against Tibet

zones.text: Shazhou, Guazhou, Ganzhou, Suzhou, Yizhou and Xizhou

wars.outcome: Zhang Yichao took the six western prefectures from the Tibetan garrisons and the Tang court named them the Guiyi Circuit in 851.
wars.note: Dates from the Guiyi page: 848 (Sha, Gua), 850 (Gan, Su, Yi), 851 (Xi); the Zhang Yichao page says only 'later in the year' 848 for the attack on ten more prefectures.

wars.name: Qocho attacks on Shazhou
wars.outcome: Qocho attacked in 869, 870 and 880 and was repelled each time; Zhang Chengfeng counter-attacked and occupied Yizhou and Xizhou in 904, an occupation the Qocho page ends in 911.
wars.note: No territorial result in 869-880; the 904 counterattack is in the ledger.

wars.name: Guiyi-Ganzhou Uyghur wars
wars.outcome: In 911 the Ganzhou Uyghurs forced the Jinshan Kingdom into a subordinate alliance; Cao Yijin 'defeated the Ganzhou Uyghurs' in 925 and married a Cao daughter to the khan in 926.
wars.note: The page gives no land changing hands.

certainty.note: Oasis and corridor frontiers with no survey or treaty line on either page; the prefecture circles are the researcher's reading.

notes:
New state (Cliopatria has no row). Open points: (1) the Tang dossier gains Shazhou, Guazhou, Ganzhou, Suzhou, Yizhou, Xizhou and Liangzhou from the Tibetans in 848-861 and then makes the Guiyi its vassal from 851; the pages read here make the Guiyi the conqueror and the Tang a nominal overlord, so those Tang gains and the Guiyi finds/gains overlap (a reviewer should pick one owner and keep the Tang vassal tint); (2) the Tibetan dossier's 861 loss of Liangzhou is 863 here (Zhang Yichao page); (3) ganzhou-kingdom founds in 894 from guiyi-circuit, whereas this page has Ganzhou slip to nobody in 881-882 and the Uyghur kingdom 'by 894'; (4) qocho-kingdom has the 866 and 876 gains from the Guiyi but no 904 loss to the Guiyi and no 914 return; (5) Lanzhou, Shanzhou, Hezhou, Minzhou, Kuozhou and Yizhou/Xizhou after 904 have no dated loss on either page (confidence 1); (6) the Ganzhou Uyghurs' superiority over the Jinshan Kingdom (911) and the Guiyi's nominal subordination to the Later Liang (918 title), the Northern Song and the Tanguts (1030) belong in the suzerains' ledgers as vassal pairs; (7) Suzhou (Jiuquan) is a coordinate circle because the gazetteer has no place of that name (listed under gazetteer_names_needed); Liangzhou is Wuwei.

Repair (2026-10-19, after review): (a) the Suzhou (Jiuquan) circle is no longer Guiyi land to the end. The Guiyi page says that 'by the end of the 10th century it was only able to keep the prefectures of Guazhou and Shazhou' and does not mention Suzhou after 850/861; a loss of Suzhou to ganzhou-kingdom is entered in 1000 at confidence 1, the dissolve region and the successor land are Shazhou and Guazhou only, and keyframe 9 is split at 1000. The Suzhou years 882-999 are a reading: no page dates the loss, the Ganzhou Uyghur Kingdom Cliopatria shape (894 on) covers the same circle, so the two dossiers draw Suzhou twice until 999 (ganzhou-kingdom's owner could carry the Suzhou gain, or its shape could be cut). (b) Yizhou and Xizhou now leave in 911, not 914, from the Qocho page's 'This occupation ended after the Jinshan Kingdom's loss to the Ganzhou Uyghur Kingdom in 911'; the 904 gain and the 911 end are typed occupation_start / occupation_end, the types qocho-kingdom uses for the same pair. (c) Still open: the Zhang Huaishen page asked for (Lanzhou, Shanzhou, Hezhou, Minzhou, Kuozhou after 882) returned not found, and the Guiyi page is silent on those five prefectures after 861, so their 882 drop stays at confidence 1.
